---

import Diagram from '../../../components/Diagram.astro';

<span class="status status--decided">decided</span>

No implementation code gets written until its behaviour is defined. The source of truth is:

- **Gherkin `.feature` files** describing behaviour in plain language
- **JSON test vectors** generated from them: an initial state, plus per-client operation streams delivered late and out of order

## One suite, every implementation

<Diagram name="13-verification" alt="Verification: feature files feed a fuzzer that emits JSON vectors; vectors run through the C++ harness and a Yrs oracle (an Elixir harness is deferred), and SHA-256 hashes of canonical XML are compared; for M1 the same vectors are replayed by C++ CLI peers through an Erlang tracker over WebSocket, with forced disconnects." />

| Harness | Why it exists |
| --- | --- |
| **C++ Xmesh (Catch2)** | The reference implementation. |
| **Elixir Xmesh (ExUnit)** | *Deferred.* If the Elixir port spike goes ahead, the same vectors become the contract it must meet. |
| **Yrs oracle** | Yrs (the Rust port of Yjs) implements YATA and is widely used. Replaying the non-move subset through it checks our YATA independently. It has no tree move, hence the subset. |

The pass condition is identical **SHA-256 hashes of the canonical XML** across every harness.

## The fuzzer

The first task from the original handover, re-scoped to feed every harness. It generates:

- an initial SVG (a root `<svg>` with one `<g>` layer)
- randomised operations from several clients: inserting paths, updating attributes, moving nodes, adding comments
- one chronological stream per client, plus heavily delayed and shuffled delivery orders

Moves are tagged so the Yrs harness can skip them.

## Over a real network

[Milestone M1](/build/milestones/) runs the same vectors through two C++ CLI peers and an Erlang tracker (driving the C++ core through a Port) over WebSocket, including dropped connections and reconnect sync. Convergence then holds over a real, unreliable network, not just in a test process.
